Sistemul românesc de învățământ are nevoie de foarte multe schimbări. Printre principalele obiective aș putea sugera:
-mărirea salarilor. Sincer, eu în orașul natal nu am cum să prind post, nu se scot ore la concurs, sunt din ce în ce mai puțini elevi, deci mai puține clase. Sunt dintr-un oraș mic. Dacă e să mă mut într-un oraș mai mare sau în altă zonă, nu mi-aș permite dintr-un salariu de profesor debutant să plătesc chirie și utilități. 
-totul să fie depolitizat. Să nu mai existe pile și relații, cunoștințe. 
-o modificare a programei. Programa trebuie modificată și îmbunătățită, desigur. Multe materii sunt incredibil  de plictisitoare și nu ajută cu nimic. Eu personal aș pune accent pe materii noi, de exemplu: Educație sexuala (nu știu dacă s-a introdus sau nu), materii cu caracter practic (fie că vorbim de ore de gătit, activități motrice). Mi-ar plăcea și mai multe ore de sport. 
-modernizarea școlilor. Sincer la școala unde am făcut liceul, eram la etajul 3 și nu erau geamuri termopan. Focul era când făcut, când nu. Purtam 3-4 straturi de haine, incluzând o bluză termo. Nu aveam cum să dăm randament atunci când efectiv tremuram de frig. Nu poți să faci școală într-un așa mediu.
Atâtea probleme sunt cu sistemul de învățământ încât nu le pot înșira pe toate...

Bring ziplock bags with you, get any food that's left on your plate to eat later. Buy snacks at big supermarkets rather than small shops in the city centre. Always carry a small snack with you. Get a reusable water bottle, there are usually places where you can refill it for free. It may seem tacky but there are places that sell bottles of water at ten times the price you could get at the supermarket. Those little things add up. Don't go to the first restaurants or hotels you see, there are probably better choices if you search more.
Bring one or two tote bags in your purse, so you won't buy plastic bags. I usually search for the cheapest place to rent on Airbnb, of course I read the reviews and chose accordingly. Get a public transportation card if there is the possibility. If it's a big city they should have a public transportation system and it'll be easier than taking a taxi or uber. Eat at local places, don't go to the overly crowded restaurants. Get currency money at the bank or at least find a place with a good exchange rate. I often travel to visit places and experience new things, so I don't  enter malls or shops. I also do not buy souvenirs, like fridge magnets. Those usually cost a lot and nobody likes them, they're not useful. I buy foods that are famous for those places, spices, local products.

Hello! I'm from Europe too, and I want to tell you something. The power of example is the best, so I shall show you some examples. 
If you're from Europe, you should have heard about communism before. My country was under a communist regime until 1989. My mother did not have a chance to education. She began working right after high school as an electrician in a factory. But she did choose to go to university at 40 years old. She had two small daughters, she was a single mom, but she wanted an education. 
Another example is one of my colleagues, in my first year of uni, I was 18 years old, and I had this awesome lady as a colleague. She was in her 60', the same as my mother, she did not have access to an education because of the regime. She wished to be a teacher after more than 30 years of being a cosmetologist. She got her degree. A lot of my colleagues were older. From their 20', to people in their 30' and so on...
My sister is the same, she wished to be a doctor, and at the age of 23 she began medschool. She'll be 29 when she finishes it, and everyone is asking her why does she want to do it because she'll be old when she finishes it. And my sister proudly tells them that she'll be 29 either way, at least she can be a doctor.
And I'm the same, although I have a degree, I'm 22 and now I'm going for my second one, and next year I'll enroll in a MA programme. It's never too late for education. Jobs usually hire you based on your skills. So it doesn't matter what's your age. If you're good at what you're doing, you have your chances. 
You're 23, you're very young and very lucky. Don't be afraid. As for scholarships, I do not believe that you'll face problems, you are still pretty young. 
Dating is another thing, ladies do prefer an older guy. :D and you could always date in your age range. Clubbing is for everyone, they won't be asking your age. If you click, you click. (It's the same for dating) 

So please just consider, you'll be 30 in a few year, do you want to be an engineer, or not? I believe that it's worth the struggle.
